2013_049_070913mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Trustees held July 9, 2013 at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. It carries consent-agenda minutes from the June 4, June 18 workshop, June 18 regular, and June 26 special meetings, teacher hires, the appointment of Joyce Brasington as Wattles Elementary principal, an MHSAA membership resolution, and bid awards for storm water work, playground surfacing, and backflow devices. The most consequential action is a resolution authorizing an Application for Preliminary Qualification of Bonds to the Michigan Department of Treasury for a School Improvement Bond issue on the November 2013 ballot.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Board of Trustees, Troy School District, July 9, 2013, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Consent agenda (Item 5)**
Minutes of the June 4, 2013 Board meeting, the June 18, 2013 workshop, the June 18, 2013 Board meeting, and the June 26, 2013 special meeting.

**June 4, 2013 minutes (Athens High School)**
Called to order 7:01 p.m.; Underwood absent; approximately 500 in the audience. A long recognition list covered All-State winter athletes, the Synchronized Swim state champions, Academic All-American golfer Jennifer Yang, MHSAA Allen W. Bush Award recipient Bob Dowd, and ASTA Elizabeth Green Award winner Alan Mac Nair. Motion 13-045 appointed Dr. Audra Melton Principal of Baker Middle School effective July 1, 2013. Numerous speakers addressed teacher negotiations and step freezes; Ms. Philippart reported a mediator had been appointed and that the TEA contract expires June 30, 2013. Motion 13-047 set a budget public hearing for June 18, 2013. Policies G-1009 and G-1010 had first readings. Adjourned 12:16 a.m.

**June 18, 2013 workshop and regular meeting**
The 6:00 p.m. workshop covered the final 2012/2013 appropriation amendment and the 2013/2014 budget; adjourned 6:46 p.m. The regular meeting opened with a budget hearing presented by Mr. Rajter, closed at 7:15 p.m. Todd Miletti received the MASB Award of Distinction; Ida Edmunds was thanked for 28 years of service.

Other June 18 actions: Superintendent's contract extended July 1, 2013 through June 30, 2016; assistant superintendent and administrator contracts extended through June 30, 2015; the TESPA agreement ratified for July 1, 2013 through June 30, 2015; Sodexo Management, Inc. food service renewal authorized; notebook computers awarded to Dell Corporation for $115,980 from the 2012-2013 General Fund, backed by roughly $125,000 in TRIG-22i funds and a $69 per-laptop rebate. Policies G-1009 and G-1010 were adopted on second reading.

**June 26, 2013 special meeting**
Convened 9:01 a.m.; Hauff and Miletti absent. Motion 13-063 ratified the TESA agreement reached June 19, 2013 for July 1, 2013 through June 30, 2015. Adjourned 9:10 a.m.

**Personnel (Item 6)**
Probationary contracts for new teachers for 2013-2014. Joyce Brasington recommended as Principal, Wattles Elementary School, effective August 6, 2013, on a two-year probationary administrative contract.

**Curriculum (Item 7)**
MHSAA membership for the district's six secondary schools, August 1, 2013 through July 31, 2014.

**Business (Item 8)**

| Bid | Award | Amount |

Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Board of Trustees of the Troy School District held July 9, 2013 at 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; the district address is 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

JUNE 4, 2013 MINUTES (Athens High School). President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. with Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, and Schmidt; Ms. Underwood was absent. Also present were Superintendent Fowler; administrators Birmingham, Dziatczak, Goss, Fulcher, Gebbie, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter, and Witt; and approximately 500 audience members. Mike Jolly and the Board recognized All-State winter athletes and the 2012-2013 Synchronized Swim Team state champions. Jennifer Yang was named a National High School Coaches Association Academic All-American in golf at Athens High School for Coach Dan Cooper, with a 4.2 GPA, ranked #1 in her class, finishing 18th in 2012 and 11th in 2013. Bob Dowd was congratulated as a 2012 recipient of the MHSAA Allen W. Bush Award, having led the Michigan Scholastic Lacrosse Association and been named Oakland County Athletic Director of the Year in 2009. Alan Mac Nair, Troy High Orchestra Conductor, received the American String Teachers Association Elizabeth Green Award in Providence, Rhode Island, and the Athens Band under Jeff McCoy performed aboard the USS Intrepid. 19 8th grade students from Boulan Park, Larson, and Smith Middle Schools earned perfect ACT Explore scores. Many further academic recognitions followed, including Safal Bora's 2nd place at the 2013 Chess Supernationals, a $1,000 Ford Foundation Grant to a Future Problem Solvers team, and the Boulan Park MathCounts team that won State at the GM Tech Center.

Motion 13-044 moved the administrative appointment ahead of public communication (Yes 6, No 0, Absent Underwood). Motion 13-045 issued a two-year probationary contract without tenure to Dr. Audra Melton as Principal, Baker Middle School, effective July 1, 2013 (Yes 6, No 0, Absent Underwood). Numerous speakers addressed teacher contract negotiations, step freezes, and performance-based pay, among them Diane Loucks, Debbie Rosenman, TEA president Tony Lucchi, and Sara Splan. Ms. Philippart reported that a mediator had been appointed as third-party negotiator, that the TEA contract expires June 30, 2013, and that the current proposal included increases over the next two years without step increases. Motion 13-047 set a public hearing on the proposed 2013/2014 budget for June 18, 2013 at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098, with notice at least six days in advance in 11-point bold faced type. First readings were given of Policy G-1009, Teacher and Administrator Evaluation (Mr. Schmidt), and Policy G-1010, Performance-Based Compensation for Teachers and Administrators (Mrs. Fleming). Motion 13-048 moved the Board into closed session on negotiations and superintendent evaluation under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c) at 10:15 p.m.; it reconvened at 10:20 p.m. and adjourned at 12:16 a.m. Minutes were submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary.

JUNE 18, 2013 WORKSHOP. Called to order 6:00 p.m. at the Services Building with all seven Board members, Superintendent Fowler, Ms. Birmingham, Mrs. Keeling, Dr. Machesky, Mrs. Papasian, Mr. Rajter, Mr. Washington, Mr. Witt, and approximately 11 audience members; covered the final 2012/2013 appropriation amendment and the 2013/2014 budget; adjourned 6:46 p.m.

JUNE 18, 2013 REGULAR MEETING. Opened 7:01 p.m. with the public hearing on the 2013-2014 proposed budget; Mr. Rajter presented tax values, homestead and non-homestead forecasts, the foundation allowance, increased student enrollment, and general fund revenues and expenditures. The hearing closed at 7:15 p.m.; all seven members were present with administrators Birmingham, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter, Washington, and Witt and approximately 200 audience members. Vice-President Todd Miletti received the MASB Award of Distinction, which requires levels 1 and 2 of advanced CBA courses and a minimum of 208 education credits; Ida Edmunds was recognized for 28 years of Board service. Motion 13-049 added Item 7.E., TESPA Contract Ratification. Speakers on merit pay and the absence criterion included Angelika Gadlage, Ben Martin, Al Merian, and Tony Lucchi. Motion 13-050 approved minutes of the May 7 meeting, the May 21 workshop, the May 28 special joint meeting with City Council and the May 28 special meeting, plus the Treasurer's Report for April and May 2013. Motion 13-051 approved Kimberly Cornelissen and Taryn Horbach-Huang. Motion 13-052 extended the Superintendent's contract from July 1, 2013 through June 30, 2016. Motion 13-053 extended through June 30, 2015 the contracts of Dr. Richard Machesky (Secondary Instruction), Jan Keeling (Elementary Instruction), Jasen Witt (Human Resources), and Mark Rajter (Business Services), and Motion 13-054 extended administrative contracts to the same date for principals and directors including Lara Dixon, Mark Dziatczak, Joe Duda, Timothy Fulcher, Michael Jolly, Kerry Birmingham, and Kenneth Miller. Motion 13-055 ratified the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA agreement reached June 4, 2013 for July 1, 2013 through June 30, 2015, and Motion 13-056 authorized the Sodexo Management, Inc. food service renewal for 2013/2014 pending Michigan Department of Education approval. Motion 13-057 amended the 2012-13 appropriations: General Fund $131,311,963; Special Revenue Funds $8,900,222; Debt Service Funds $61,504,693; Capital Projects Maintenance Fund $195,008; Internal Service Fund $25,000. Motion 13-058 approved the 2013-14 appropriations and millage rates: General Fund $130,730,672; Special Revenue Funds $8,333,083; Debt Service funds $12,287,912; Capital Project/Capital Projects Maintenance Funds shown with a dash; Internal Service Funds $25,000; Non-Homestead general operating 18.0000 mills; Commercial Personal Property general operating 11.3741 mills; Homestead general operating 5.3741 mills; All Properties debt retirement 4.7000 mills. Motion 13-059 awarded the notebook computer bid to Dell Corporation for $115,980 from the 2012-2013 General Fund; the District was awarded approximately $125,000 from the Technology Readiness Infrastructure Grant (TRIG)-22i through the Michigan Department of Education, with a $69 rebate per laptop off the state bid, for one year. Teri Crandall and Dorothea Stevenson raised safety concerns at Hamilton Elementary, including a filed police report. Motions 13-060 and 13-061 adopted Policies G-1009 and G-1010 on second reading. Motion 13-062 moved the Board into closed session on negotiations at 9:06 p.m.; it reconvened at 9:09 p.m. and adjourned at 10:34 p.m. Every June 18 vote was recorded Yes 7, No 0.

JUNE 26, 2013 SPECIAL MEETING (Administration Building). Called to order 9:01 a.m. with Philippart, Edmunds, Fleming, Schmidt, and Underwood; Hauff and Miletti absent; Superintendent Fowler and administrators Keeling, Machesky, Rajter, and Witt; approximately 3 audience members. Motion 13-063 ratified the tentative agreement reached June 19, 2013 with the Troy Educational Secretarial Association/MEA/NEA for July 1, 2013 through June 30, 2015 (Yes 5, No 0, Absent Hauff and Miletti). Adjourned 9:10 a.m.

PERSONNEL (Item 6.A). Probationary contracts recommended for 2013-2014: Lindsey Becker, 1.0 FTE Mathematics, Baker Middle School; Emily Burzynski, 1.0 FTE Social Worker, Services Building; Claire Castine, Fourth Grade, Barnard Elementary; Elizabeth Crawford, .5 FTE Developmental Kindergarten, Leonard Elementary; Christina DePassio, 1.0 FTE Elementary PE, school TBD; Lauren Hilliker, .7 FTE Elementary Art (Visual Arts in her biographical sketch), school TBD; Katherine Niedbala, 1.0 FTE Elementary PE, school TBD; Lori Opron, Wass Elementary; Rachel Weiner, Fourth Grade, Hamilton Elementary; Samantha Feldman, 1.0 FTE English, Troy High School; Melissa Zwolinski, 1.0 FTE History, International Academy Central. Biographical sketches list degrees from Oakland University, Central Michigan University, the University of Michigan, and Grand Valley State University.

PERSONNEL (Item 6.B). Recommendation to appoint Ms. Joyce Brasington as Principal, Wattles Elementary School, on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure effective August 6, 2013. She comes from Oxford Community School District, where she was Principal at Daniel Axford Elementary School for four years, previously Principal at Leonard Elementary School for four years, Assistant Principal at Oxford Middle School for five years, and a math teacher and counselor for five years. She holds a Bachelor of Science in Secondary Education (1987), a Master of Education in Guidance and Counseling (1991), and an Education Specialist degree in Administration (1997).

CURRICULUM (Item 7.A). Resolution continuing Michigan High School Athletic Association membership, enrolling the six secondary schools of the Troy School District, City of Troy, County of Oakland, from August 1, 2013 through July 31, 2014, delegating supervision to the Superintendent or designee and adopting the MHSAA Constitution, By-Laws, and Handbook.

BUSINESS (Item 8.A). Resolution authorizing the Superintendent to file an Application for Preliminary Qualification of Bonds with the Michigan Department of Treasury under the Michigan School Bond Qualification and Loan Program, contemplating voter-approved capital improvement bonds for a School Improvement Bond issue on the November 2013 ballot, with a final qualification application to follow voter approval. The certification recites action on the 9th day of July, 2013 under Act 276 of the Public Acts of 1976. Listed are Paula Fleming, Secretary; Mark Rajter, Treasurer; Dr. Barbara Fowler, Superintendent of Schools; bond counsel Clark Hill of Birmingham, MI 48009; financial consultant Stauder, Barch & Associates, 3899 Research Park Dr., Ann Arbor, MI 48108; architect TMP Architecture, 1191 W. Square Lake Road, Bloomfield Hills, MI 48302; and construction manager Barton Malow Company, 26500 American Drive, Southfield, MI 48034.

BUSINESS (Item 8.B, Bid 9761). Storm water system maintenance and repairs recommended for award to Power Vac of Michigan, Inc. for $80,680.00 from the 2013-2014 General Fund; invitations went to 10 potential bidders with 1 responding. A July 1, 2013 memorandum from Kenneth D. Miller, Executive Director, Facility Operations & Purchasing, 1140 Rankin, Troy, Michigan 48083, to Mark Rajter cites EPA and MDEQ storm water mandates and a two-week newspaper advertisement. The tabulation shows cleaning at $30,680.00 and repairs at $50,000.00, noting concealed conditions below the waterline may increase expense, totaling $80,680.00.

BUSINESS (Item 8.C, Bid 9762). Playground loose fill surfacing material and installation recommended for award to Rolar Property Service, Inc. for $79,400.00 from the 2013-2014 General Fund; 9 bidders invited, 3 responding. Miller's July 1, 2013 memorandum notes Consumer Product Safety Commission regulations require a minimum of 12 inches of loose fill in playground drop zone areas, maintained annually. Tabulation: Interlake Landscaping Services, Inc. $85,400.00; Michigan Recreational Contruction, Inc. $157,150.00; Rolar Property Service, Inc. $79,400.00.

BUSINESS (Item 8.D, Bid 9763). Backflow devices rebuilt and/or replaced recommended for award to Power Vac of Michigan, Inc. for $29,090.00 from the 2013-2014 General Fund; 10 bidders invited, 2 responding, one incomplete. Miller's July 2, 2013 memorandum states backflow regulators are required by city code and that Cregger Mechanical Systems, Inc.'s proposal lacked the required proposal form, the Sworn and Notarized Familial Disclosure Statement, the Certification of Compliance - Iran Economic Sanctions Act (Michigan Public Act No. 517 of 2012), the Acceptance of Proposal Document, and the tabulation sheet.

CLOSED SESSION (Item 11.A). Resolution to go into closed session to discuss negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), by roll call of Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, and Schmidt, with no additional business other than adjournment.
